summary: Refused at Step 6 (template-class provenance) before emitting any class. Three of the five canonical templates this step's templates[] mandates - TriggerHandler.cls, BaseService.cls and HttpClient.cls - cannot be shipped into this build: each one references a further templates/apex class that no step of this plan ships, and those classes in turn require custom objects and custom metadata types that no step of this plan ships either. HttpClient.send()/sendOnce() call ApplicationLogger.warn/error; BaseService.logAndRethrow()/logAndSwallow() call ApplicationLogger.error; ApplicationLogger writes Application_Log__c rows and reads Logger_Setting__mdt.getInstance('Default'), and clarification Q16 answered that the org has no Apex log object. TriggerHandler.run() calls TriggerControl.isActive(), TriggerControl is a canonical template this step's templates[] does not even list, and TriggerControl.getCache() queries Trigger_Setting__mdt. The 2026-09-12T10:51:56Z amendment set include_logger false and removed templates/apex/ApplicationLogger.cls from templates[], which closes the logger for the classes this agent writes but not for the three templates it is required to compose them from - so inputs.callout_endpoint ('composed through templates/apex/HttpClient.cls') and inputs.logging_decision_2026_09_12 ('Do not reference ApplicationLogger') cannot both be satisfied. Zero files were written under artefacts/M1-S03/.
confidence_rationale: LOW per GATES.md Gate D: the run refused, no package was emitted, and no compile check ran (build_mode is design-only, no target_org_alias). The refusal itself rests on direct reads of the four template files and the two upstream steps' artefacts rather than on inference.

refusal.message: agents/apex-builder/AGENT.md Step 6 template-class provenance: every templates/apex/** class an emitted class or test references must be shipped in this step's outputs as a verbatim copy plus its -meta.xml, or already declared by an earlier plan step. Three mandated templates fail that test transitively and no step of this plan declares the classes or the metadata they need. (1) templates/apex/HttpClient.cls lines 67 and 96 call ApplicationLogger.warn / ApplicationLogger.error. (2) templates/apex/BaseService.cls lines 45 and 50 call ApplicationLogger.error. (3) templates/apex/ApplicationLogger.cls constructs Application_Log__c records and calls Logger_Setting__mdt.getInstance('Default'); neither exists in this build - M1-S01 ships Integration_Failure__c, Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c and Tier2_Escalation__e only, and Q16 answered 'We have no existing Apex log object in the org'. (4) templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls line 38 calls TriggerControl.isActive(sObjectName, handlerName); templates/apex/TriggerControl.cls is not in this step's templates[], is shipped by no step, and its getCache() queries Trigger_Setting__mdt, which is shipped by no step. Shipping a caller without its template fails deploy with 'Variable does not exist: ApplicationLogger' / 'Variable does not exist: TriggerControl'; shipping ApplicationLogger contradicts inputs.logging_decision_2026_09_12, which the requester and the dry-run operator settled at 2026-09-12T10:51:56Z after exactly this finding on M1-S04.
refusal.remediation_hint: A human chooses between two amendments; this agent does not choose. (A) Add an Apex-foundations step - the shape standards/build-orchestration.md section 4 Apex-row note prescribes when more than one Apex step shares a template dependency - owned by metadata-builder, shipping templates/apex/custom_objects/Application_Log__c and its fields, templates/apex/cmdt/Logger_Setting__mdt and its Minimum_Severity__c field plus a Default record, and templates/apex/cmdt/Trigger_Setting__mdt and its three fields; M1-S03 then depends_on it and ships TriggerHandler, TriggerControl, BaseService, HttpClient and ApplicationLogger verbatim. This re-opens Q16, whose answer was about where failures are visible to Support Engineering rather than about whether a framework log table may exist, and it adds a sixth functional step to a feature-tier plan. (B) amend-step this step's templates[] and inputs.callout_endpoint to drop TriggerHandler.cls, BaseService.cls and HttpClient.cls and authorise build-local, dependency-free equivalents grounded in the cited skills' references/code-examples.md, declaring each new .cls and -meta.xml in outputs[]; this contradicts decision D4, which mandates HttpClient, so D4 is revisited in the same amendment. Considered and rejected: shipping a class named ApplicationLogger or TriggerControl that is not byte-identical to the canonical template - the provenance rule requires verbatim, and a same-named divergent copy misleads every later reader.

process_observations.observation: The two templates this step mandates for tests - MockHttpResponseGenerator.cls and TestDataFactory.cls - are self-contained: neither references another templates/apex class and neither names a custom object or custom metadata type, so the test half of this step has no provenance problem at all.

All three declared checkers exit 0 against the five mandated template files, so nothing in the templates themselves trips the acceptance tests this step declares - the blocker is compile-time and metadata-shaped, which static text checkers cannot see.

process_observations.observation: The 2026-09-12T10:51:56Z amendment fixed the logger dependency at the level of include_logger, which governs the classes apex-builder writes, but three of the five templates it left in templates[] carry the same dependency one level down - so the amendment was sufficient for M1-S04 (templates[] is now TestDataFactory.cls alone, self-contained) and insufficient for M1-S03, which is the only step whose templates[] carries TriggerHandler, BaseService and HttpClient.

templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls cannot compile without templates/apex/TriggerControl.cls, but this step's templates[] lists TriggerHandler without TriggerControl - a template pairing that is invisible to plan-time validation because build_plan.py validate confirms each cited template path exists and does not read the file for its own references.

M1-S02's Named Credential Url parameter already carries the full path /v1/salesforce/escalations, while inputs.callout_endpoint describes the endpoint as 'callout:OnCall_Tool plus a path' - so whether any path segment should be appended at all is unsettled, and appending one would post to /v1/salesforce/escalations/<segment>.
Once a human picks remedy A or B, the plan change is an amend-step on a step that is currently blocked, which build-planner rather than this agent owns.
process_observations.followup_reason: because the remedy is a change to templates[], inputs and possibly a new Apex-foundations step, which is plan authorship rather than scaffold emission.
